pull.title: [RFC] enable `clang-tidy` `optin.performance.Padding`
pull.body:
Enable `optin.performance.Padding` with the default of 24 bytes (made explicit in the clang-tidy config), after fixing warnings for more padding than that. Enabling it at this point would be to catch regressions above this amount.

Based on #36501, which reorders `CBlockIndex` to save 8 bytes (`clang-tidy` also warns about this). Wondering if contributors/reviewers think this is worthwhile given we may make that refactor? Also not sure if it's possible for us to enable this generally, as padding will differ depending on various factors.

Reorder CBlockIndex members to save 8 bytes

On a windows x64 build, CBlockIndex size is 160 bytes. Moving one field
somewhere else makes the class lose less bytes due to padding to respect
the 8-byte alignment

For a ~1M block height, this saves about 8M of Ram without doing
anything else.

Concept ACK, seems worthwhile to me.

Concept ACK, modulo consider keeping guarded members near their mutex and avoiding churn or grouping members less logically where it provides negligible benefit (arguably the changes in rpc/client.cpp and txmempool.h).

Concept ACK, probably good to turn this on by default with a reasonable threshold.

For singleton types (`*Man` etc), in cases where it really leads to less logical groupings of fields, one could opt out, like we do for recursion warnings today.

Concept ACK for me too. I had not included other classes in the original PR because they are probably instantiated far less than 1 million times at once, so the changes seemed not worth it to me (sometimes members are ordered by fonctionality, code might be more understandable that way). But if there is now a CI check to avoid potentially losing more memory in the future, I'm all for it.

It seems the limit of 23 is not properly used though, since the CI output warns about a loss of 11 padding bytes?
